newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senator Lott wants panel to fix CPI bias.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senator Lott wants panel to fix CPI bias.

text.p: U.S. Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said Monday he favors creation of a commission to correct any bias in the government's chief inflation gauge, the Consumer Price Index.
Lott told a meeting of the National Association of Broadcasters that later this week, he will call for establishment of such a panel that will bw made up of a small group of "gray beards."
The Mississippi Republican said he favors Congress fixing the CPI, which a government-appointed panel recently concluded overstated the annual inflation rate by 1.1 percentage points.
Lott did not offer details about the panel, saying only that it would take input from Congress and other sources while trying to determine how and whether to adjust the CPI.
Asked whether the CPI should be adjusted to correct any bias, Lott responded, "I think it should be."
He added: "If the number is correct, leave it alone. If it's understated, fix it. If it's overstated, fix it."
Lott suggested the size of the CPI panel would number just four people. He said he favored Congress moving on the issue this year.

Any downward adjustment in the CPI could save the government billions of dollars in Social Security payments, which are pegged to the CPI. Individual tax brackets also are pegged to the inflation index.
